help: AI assistants reflexively prefix comments with NOTE/IMPORTANT/CAREFUL/CRITICAL/TIP/HACK to signal importance. Real human code rarely does this; the label is decorative, not load-bearing. Strip the prefix and let the comment speak for itself, or delete the comment entirely if it adds nothing the next line doesn't already say.

AI generates section banners like `# ====== SECTION 1 ======` to visually segment code that should be split into functions or modules instead. The banner is a smell that the surrounding code is too long. Either delete the banner and let the code stand on its own, or extract the section into a named function.

message: AI hedge or self-reference leaked into a code comment.
help: `# Note: this assumes...` and `# As an AI, I cannot...` are AI hedging that escaped into source. Either capture the assumption as an assertion (`assert x is not None, ...`) and remove the comment, or document the real precondition in a docstring. AI self-references should never appear in shipped code.

AI assistants praise their own output in comments: 'Pythonic', 'idiomatic', 'elegant', 'clean code', 'robust', 'comprehensive'. These are vocabulary tells, not facts. Real code either is good or isn't; the comment doesn't change that. Strip the praise; if the comment has no other content, delete it.

message: Emoji in source code (comment, identifier, or operator position).
help: AI assistants sprinkle emojis into comments and identifiers (`# ✅ done`, `def hello_🎉():`) — a strong AI fingerprint. Emojis in string literals (CLI output, user-facing text) are not flagged; those are intentional UX. Remove the emoji from the comment; if the comment becomes empty, delete the line.
